Extract CoS simply change the coverage without checking purity

Source: R/colocboost_output.R
get_cos.Rd

get_cos get the colocalization confidence sets (CoS) with different coverage.

Usage

get_cos(cb_output, coverage = 0.95)

Arguments

cb_output

Output object from colocboost analysis

coverage

A number between 0 and 1 specifying the “coverage” of the estimated colocalization confidence sets (CoS) (default is 0.95).

Value

A list of indices of variables in each CoS.

See also

Other colocboost_utilities: get_cormat()

Examples

# colocboost example
set.seed(1)
N <- 1000
P <- 100
# Generate X with LD structure
sigma <- 0.9^abs(outer(1:P, 1:P, "-"))
X <- MASS::mvrnorm(N, rep(0, P), sigma)
colnames(X) <- paste0("SNP", 1:P)
L <- 3
true_beta <- matrix(0, P, L)
true_beta[10, 1] <- 0.5 # SNP10 affects trait 1
true_beta[10, 2] <- 0.4 # SNP10 also affects trait 2 (colocalized)
true_beta[50, 2] <- 0.3 # SNP50 only affects trait 2
true_beta[80, 3] <- 0.6 # SNP80 only affects trait 3
Y <- matrix(0, N, L)
for (l in 1:L) {
  Y[, l] <- X %*% true_beta[, l] + rnorm(N, 0, 1)
}
res <- colocboost(X = X, Y = Y)
#> Starting checking the input data.
#> Starting gradient boosting algorithm.
#> Boosting iterations for outcome 1 converge after 98 iterations!
#> Boosting iterations for outcome 3 converge after 106 iterations!
#> Boosting iterations for outcome 2 converge after 107 iterations!
#> Starting assemble analyses and results summary.
get_cos(res, coverage = 0.75)
#> $`cos1:y1_y2`
#> [1] 10
#>
